views.visible: Geonosis establishing view: tapering hive spires rise from layered footings in a much wider dusty plain.
views.subject: settlement-edge
views.settingCue: Ground stays open between groups of spires; the apron grades straight into rock rather than forming a paved city grid.

views.visible: Geonosis arena exterior court: stacked curved tiers sit inside the excavated red rock above a comparatively smooth open floor.
views.subject: building
views.settingCue: The decorated columns and inhabited tiers have deliberate boundaries. Their wall texture is not a repeating street material.
views.nativeContext: Distant Geonosian spectators give scale to the depth of the curved tiers; no individual is the subject.

views.visible: Official Weapons Factory concept view: the crevasse bridge lands on an irregular ledge among hive towers with bare ground beyond.
views.subject: settlement-edge
views.settingCue: Carry the eroded bed up to an actual structure. The bridge is a settlement-edge reference, not permission to add a bridge to this board.

views.visible: Earth analogue, NPS Badlands: ledges stack below an isolated summit and break into shadowed gullies.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: A resistant bed can carry sideways to form a short bench before a saddle interrupts it. The rainbow is not a weather instruction.

views.visible: Earth analogue, NPS Badlands: loose angular blocks accumulate along a paler crumbling shoulder.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: Concentrate coarse lag where the scarp sheds material. Do not import the photographed shrubs or pale rock color.

views.visible: Earth analogue, BLM Kasha-Katuwe: a cut bank resolves into fluted faces and free-standing cones beside a narrow wash.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: Shallow tops and steep faces read at different scales. The cones are erosion evidence, not Geonosian buildings.

views.visible: Earth analogue, Golden Canyon: overlapping dissected slopes open onto a broad fine-grained fan beneath distant ridges.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: The gap between distant ridges matters as much as their height. Do not enclose the map within one continuous wall.

views.visible: Earth analogue, Golden Canyon: the broad shadowed wash has parallel runs of coarse sediment surrounded by fine ground.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: Change the grain of the floor inside the same channel without painting a sharp border between shade and sun.

views.visible: Earth analogue, Golden Canyon: the narrow floor bends out of sight under two close, sharply eroded walls.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: Keep a fine, traversable strip at the foot of even a steep rock wall rather than projecting bare cliff across the entire bed.

views.visible: Earth analogue, BLM Bisti/De-Na-Zin: low capstones overhang narrower bases above a coarse, level floor.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: An eroded shoulder opens onto a debris fan without alternating between sand dunes and masonry. The grey stone is not a color target.

ground.decision: Carry fine ochre sediment through open washes. Scoured crust and angular fan gravel give way to exposed rock on the scarps.
ground.reject: Not loose dune sand everywhere, alternating brick paving at every tower-textured vertex, or map-wide orange lighting baked into the albedo.

foliage.decision: Keep the dry flats, fissures and hive shoulders free of remaster vegetation. All eight mounted prop models are mineral, architecture or vents.
foliage.reject: Do not transplant Earth brush or a decorative cover layer into this treeless board.

review.basis: The mounted scene has 681 clustered rock placements, 16 larger rock forms, 21 tower models and 23 fissure or steam placements; none is a plant. The cited Geonosis basin view has an open sediment floor.

exclude.where: Across the basin, hive approaches, steam fissures and the outer tableland.
exclude.reason: Exposed mineral ground connects the shelves with no observed planted zone.

variation.decision: Vary the size and exposure of mineral deposits, not plant species or planting density.
limits: Allocate no remaster plant, crown, grass or horizon-tree layer.

landmark.decision: Keep the actual tapering tower spires, natural rock forms and eastern fissure at their authored silhouettes and positions. Sediment reaches the foot of the towers.
landmark.reject: Do not rebuild the film arena or foundry in this skirmish board, import Earth buildings, or grade the map to a movie frame.

natural.decision: Fine sediment and eroded hardpan meet rocky escarpments. Pale mineral traces in surveyed dry channels are not snow, water or a permanent river.

built.decision: The authored tower model provides the built boundary. No paved streets at the spire bases: slot 62 alone may acquire concrete through an actual construction receipt.

transition.decision: Continue the local dusty apron to a hive wall; gravel and broken stone build near a change of grade rather than following a circular stamp around every prop.

outskirts.skyline: Uneven, broad-topped rock benches with low gaps carry the canyon country beyond the playable rim. The actual Geonosian spires remain the architectural landmarks.
outskirts.join: Start at the 1,240 authored rim vertices and copy seam heights, normals and cover. Carry loose and scoured deposits a short way out before the mantle thins on rocky steps.
outskirts.reject: No evergreen fringe, repeated needle wall, invented arena towers or uniform sand dunes on the horizon.

climate.substrate: Fine dust, firm broken crust and patchy washed gravel belong to one continuous mineral floor on both sides of the board.
climate.lighting: Keep all three authored clear skies, their orange volcanic light and planet rings. The TED names no precipitation scenario; do not stage rain or sandstorms.
climate.exceptions: Allow light on tilted faces, shadows at spire feet and subtle mineral deposits in dry channels. Preserve cliff exposures rather than covering them in red silt.

pairs.basis: Two open floor windows just above the deployed western infantry, clear of the outlying rubble cluster and the spire on the scarp.
Two sediment windows west of the standing tower in the eastern wash, outside its shadow, rock clusters, unit silhouettes and HUD.

uncertain: Reference spires and physical badland analogues establish a ground-to-wall relationship and erosion forms, not the location of fictional rooms, exact minerals, or a mandate to build another settlement.
